name: Centro Historico
tagline: The colonial heart around the plaza
description: The postcard core of Barichara, a grid of whitewashed adobe walls and cobbled streets ringed around the main plaza and its honey-coloured sandstone cathedral. Cafes, artisan workshops and guesthouses sit within an easy stroll here.
bestFor: Visitors wanting beauty, walkability and cafe life at the town's heart
pros: Best choice of cafes and eateries

name: Capilla de Santa Barbara viewpoint area
tagline: Quiet lanes near the famous overlook
description: The calm northern edge of town around the little Capilla de Santa Barbara, where a small park and mirador open onto sweeping views over the Suarez canyon country. Streets here feel peaceful, residential and gently removed from the plaza bustle.
bestFor: Those craving canyon views, calm evenings and unhurried residential quiet

name: Camino Real edge toward Guane
tagline: Town's edge where the trail begins
description: The western fringe of Barichara where the cobbled grid gives way to the historic Camino Real footpath winding down to tiny Guane. It is airy, semi-rural and green, favoured by walkers and anyone wanting space and open horizons.
bestFor: Hikers and nature lovers wanting trail access and open, green surrounds
pros: Direct access to the Camino Real to Guane
Great for daily walks and fresh air

name: Guane village
tagline: Tiny hamlet at the trail's end
description: A sleepy little village a short walk or drive from Barichara, reached along the Camino Real. Guane offers a modest plaza, a small church and fossil museum, and a deeply slow rural rhythm well beyond even Barichara's calm pace.
bestFor: Anyone seeking deep quiet, rural authenticity and total escape from crowds
